one_line.text: Stanford organisational-behaviour professor emeritus and psychologist who studies why ideas spread, how decisions fail, and how messages can be designed to stick.

biography.text: Heath is the Thrive Foundation for Youth Professor of Organizational Behavior, Emeritus, at Stanford Graduate School of Business. He earned a bachelor's degree in industrial engineering from Texas A&M and a doctorate in psychology from Stanford, and previously taught at Chicago and Duke. His academic work appears in psychology, economics, consumer-behaviour, strategy, and organisational journals.

background.text: His research asks why some ideas survive in a social marketplace, how messages can be made memorable, and how people and organisations make important decisions. He has taught organisational behaviour, negotiation, strategy, and social entrepreneurship and has worked with his brother Dan to turn behavioural research into applied frameworks.

expertise.text: Chip Heath has direct academic expertise in psychology, organisational behaviour, decision-making, and idea transmission. The Power of Moments ranges beyond this evidence into service design, education, relationships, health care, and family life, where the examples demonstrate possibilities more often than controlled outcomes.

perspective_and_limits.text: His approach favours memorable categories, case studies, and practical design prompts. That makes research usable but can make a framework look more unified and causal than the underlying studies warrant. As a business-school scholar writing with a case writer, he gives organisations and leaders more space than power differences, culture, trauma, or recipients who do not want an experience engineered for them.
